comments.body:
So... technically this is invalid code. `inout` parameters are copied in and copied out, which means that without initializing `tex` to a value in all control paths the function writes an undefined value back to `tex2d` on function exit. While technically the undefined behavior should be optimized away during inlining because you always check the result of `getTextureFromId`, the language is a bit vague.

There also seems to be a bug here between SM 6.5 and SM 6.6. The code compiles successfully under SM 6.6. @pow2clk suggested this is because of the resource handle annotations that were added in 6.6. I think it is correct that DXIL Condense Resources is incorrectly not identifying that the resource value is unknown on SM 6.6, and that is probably because the pass isn't looking through the handle annotations.

The general gist of what happens is that the control flow is getting reduced oddly in the optimizer (I don't even think the resulting control flow is correct). This results in the value of `tex2d` at the `SampleGrad` call either being `undef` or `NonUniformResourceIndex(max((int)textureId - 1, 0))`. A sample call on an `undef` is invalid. The offending IR is:

```llvm
%2 = phi i32 [ %IMax, %if.end.9.i.i ], [ undef, %entry ]
```

I totally understand that the undefined behavior in this code _should_ be optimizable, so we _should_ reduce this. DXC doesn't, and the undefined behavior in the shader results in invalid DXIL.

We have two separate issues to resolve here:
1. SM 6.6 should also be failing based on the current IR generation, but isn't. We should fix that since it causes correctness bugs.
2. On all shader models we should be able to fully flatten the control flow and eliminate the `phi`.
